newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia helps jittery Helsinki to partial recovery.
newsitem.headline: Nokia helps jittery Helsinki to partial recovery.

text.p: A rally in telecom group Nokia helped shares end up but well off highs on Tuesday, partly patching up Monday's losses but with the market still queasy after Wall Street's Friday plunge, operators said.

The FOX portfolio index closed 0.67 percent higher at 1,192.07, but off an intraday high of 1,198.08 points and only recouping part of Monday's 1.8 percent drop. The all-share HEX rose 1.17 percent to 3,491.80 points.
Volume was sturdy at almost 800 million markka.
"Sentiment is cautiously positive," one market analyst said, but added that the correction may not be over yet.
"The fact that volume was modest for most of the day in shares other than Nokia shows that domestic investors are still very cautious," one broker said.
"After such volatility in the Dow, the market will take things one day at a time," he added.
Nokia most-traded A share ended 8.90 markka higher at 454.90, and Nokia K rose 11.00 markka to 456.00.
Together the two shares accounted for about a third of total bourse volume and supplied more than six points of the eight-point rise in the FOX index.
Cargo equipment and building materials group Partek closed up 4.30 markka at 94.10 after hitting 96.00 on news it will buy 51 percent of Swedish Kalmar Industries.

"This was good news," one broker said of Partek's plan to buy a majority stake in Kalmar by merging its Sisu Terminal Systems unit with the Swedish group to create what it called the world's leading company in container-handling machines.
Retailer Stockmann added 16.00 markka to end at 288.00 after it reported first-half pre-tax earnings up 46 percent to 162 million markka.

Raisio gained 15.00 markka, closing at 550.00 after it said it had won U.S. government approval for its deal with a unit of U.S. consumer goods giant Johnson & Johnson to use its stanol ester fat product in North America.

Brokers said investors broadly expected the U.S. Federal Reserve later on Tuesday to leave key interest rates unchanged, and that such an announcement would help ease tension but not necessarily halt the correction in the U.S. stock market.
